`hermes-completed.json` records the native Hermes API adapter, AIAgent and SessionDB against our loopback model simulator (`hermes_context_contract.py`), captured from Hermes commit `fe04d5b36de1bc2d69d91185f4955c37aaef8c39`. It contains only synthetic text. Talaria plugin 1.3.0 omits the native `reasoning.available` prose preview; genuine reasoning is tested separately through the provider callback. Ephemeral status notices, provider metadata, timing and identifiers are excluded by an explicit field allowlist.

`hermes-tools.json`, `hermes-interrupted.json`, and `hermes-failure.json` were captured from Hermes commit `205645ee424163c7b6cfc032c331c3557797497b`. They exercise real provider reasoning, a clarification tool round, stopping during that tool, and an HTTP 400 provider failure. Only synthetic content and allowlisted contract fields are recorded; generated clarification IDs and interruption elapsed time are normalized.

The native contract compares fresh captures against these fixtures for both providers. Browser tests replay them with batched and fragmented delivery, reload the saved session, and send a follow-up. They cover specific native sequences, alongside broader constructed regressions. Review contract drift before deliberately updating a fixture; never automatically accept new snapshots.
